summary: Retires the Compass assistant's storage: a database migration permanently drops the compass_threads and compass_thread_messages tables (all saved Compass assistant conversations) and removes the 'compass_enabled' flag from every organization's feature settings; the matching models are deleted. No remaining code reads these tables.

statements.why: The deletion is intentional cleanup of a retired feature and the card's ship steps disclose that data is deleted; no access/money/secret issues.

statements.text: Most of this change is in a new file, server/migrations/versions/2026-10-30-1100_drop_compass.py (173 lines added).
statements.why: New migration (182 lines, 173 non-blank); doesn't say what it removes.

statements.text: The agent also deleted server/polar/models/compass_thread.py and server/polar/models/compass_thread_message.py.
Apply the migration to your live database before the new code goes live (`alembic upgrade head`), or the parts that use it will fail.
statements.why: This migration only drops tables nothing uses anymore (git grep finds no CompassThread users outside migrations); the new code doesn't depend on it, so nothing fails if it runs later. For a drop, running it after the code ships is the safe order.

statements.text: Back up your data first: the migration deletes data and can't be undone.
statements.why: drop_table removes all Compass conversations; downgrade only recreates empty tables.

misses.what: The data being deleted is every saved Compass assistant conversation (threads and messages) for all organizations, and the 'compass_enabled' setting is wiped from all organizations (so any org with the split Billing/Compass/Customers navigation turned on loses it).
